title: Reconcile prefix cache vs KV cache metric naming (standards + ADR alignment)
author: Nadia Rahman
release_notes: - Telemetry: cache metrics renamed to match observability standards and ADR definitions; legacy metric names remain temporarily as deprecated aliases (see runbook/docs for mapping).
body:
## Summary
This PR reconciles naming between "prefix cache" vs "KV cache" metrics in the serving runtime and standardizes metric + label names to match:
- Observability standards: `cache-metrics-naming-and-cardinality-policy`
- ADR: `adr-prefix-kv-cache-hit-rate-definition`

Net effect: dashboards/alerts can rely on one stable namespace and avoid ambiguous (and occasionally inverted) terminology that crept in across earlier instrumentation PRs.

## Motivation / context
During ENG-4821 review + early dashboard wireframes, we found:
- Some metrics used `prefix_cache_*` for what was actually KV reuse (post-prefill), while others used `kv_cache_*` for prefix reuse during prefill.
- Counters were inconsistently suffixed (`_count` vs `_total`) and gauges used mixed units.
- Label keys drifted (`model` vs `model_id`, `route` vs `route_id`, `deployment` vs `deployment_mode`).

This made it hard to build consistent panels and also complicated ingestion-side allowlists and drop rules.

## What changed
### 1) Metric namespaces and canonical names
We now use two explicit top-level families:
- `redwood.runtime.cache.prefix.*` for prefix/prompt reuse during prefill
- `redwood.runtime.cache.kv.*` for KV reuse effectiveness during decode (and related capacity/pressure signals)

Canonical examples:
- `redwood.runtime.cache.prefix.reused_tokens_total`
- `redwood.runtime.cache.prefix.requests_with_reuse_total`
- `redwood.runtime.cache.kv.hit_tokens_total`
- `redwood.runtime.cache.kv.miss_tokens_total`
- `redwood.runtime.cache.kv.miss_tokens_total{miss_reason=...}`
- `redwood.runtime.cache.kv.evictions_total{eviction_reason=...}`
- `redwood.runtime.cache.kv.memory_pressure_ratio` (gauge in [0,1])
- `redwood.runtime.cache.wasted_prefill_tokens_total` (cross-cutting; kept outside prefix/kv to match earlier dashboard spec)

### 2) Label key normalization
Aligned to standards doc and gateway join keys:
- `deployment_mode`: hosted | dedicated | private
- `region`: e.g. us-east-1
- `model_id`, `model_version`
- `route_id`
- `prompt_length_bucket`: small fixed set (e.g. 0_256, 257_1024, 1025_4096, 4097_plus)

No behavioral changes to allowlists here; this PR just ensures runtime emits the canonical keys that ingestion expects.

### 3) Deprecation / compatibility plan
Legacy metric names remain emitted as *deprecated aliases* for a limited time:
- Runtime will emit both canonical + legacy names for **2 release trains** (or 30 days in hosted, whichever is longer), guarded by `cache_telemetry.emit_legacy_names=true` (default: true in prod for now).
- New names are always emitted when cache telemetry is enabled.
- Legacy names are annotated in docs as deprecated; dashboards should migrate ASAP.

Deprecation mapping (non-exhaustive, see `docs/internal/telemetry/cache_metrics_migration.md` for full list):
- `redwood.cache.kv.hit_rate` -> `redwood.runtime.cache.kv.hit_tokens_total` + `...miss_tokens_total` (hit-rate computed in queries)
- `redwood.cache.prefix.hit_count` -> `redwood.runtime.cache.prefix.requests_with_reuse_total`
- `redwood.cache.prefix.reuse_depth` -> `redwood.runtime.cache.prefix.reused_tokens_total` (depth now represented via histogram in separate PR; this PR aligns the family name)

Rationale: standards prefer emitting the raw totals/histograms and computing derived ratios in dashboards/queries to avoid confusion around partial-hit semantics.

## Files / areas touched (high level)
- `runtime/telemetry/cache_metrics.*`: renamed instruments + label keys
- `runtime/telemetry/metrics_registry.*`: added alias helper for temporary legacy emission
- `runtime/config/cache_telemetry_flags.*`: `emit_legacy_names` flag + docs
- `docs/internal/telemetry/cache_metrics_migration.md`: mapping table + timeline
- `tests/integration/cache_metrics_*`: updated assertions to check canonical names; retained one test that asserts legacy aliases still show up when enabled

## Testing
- Unit tests updated for canonical metric keys
- Integration test: `CacheMetricsEmitBothNamesWhenLegacyEnabled` verifies both are present
- Validated locally with `telemetry_smoke` target (ensures ingestion schema accepts new label keys)

CI:
- build-runtime: pass
- runtime-unit: pass
- runtime-integration: pass
- lint: pass

## Notes for dashboard/alert owners
- Please update queries to new names. Legacy names will remain for a short window but should not be relied on.
- This PR intentionally does *not* change sampling; see PR-18425 for sampling/rate-limits.

## Review discussion highlights
- Omar El-Sayed: requested we avoid the term "hit_rate" for raw metrics and compute ratios in dashboards to align with ADR partial-hit semantics. Updated accordingly; removed `*_hit_rate` gauges.
- Allison Grant: asked for an explicit migration doc + timeline. Added `cache_metrics_migration.md` and release note.
- Caleb Johnson: confirmed label key normalization is compatible with ingestion allowlists; requested we do not introduce per-tenant labels here. No tenant labels added.

## Checklist
- [x] Names aligned to standards + ADR
- [x] Legacy aliases gated and time-bounded
- [x] Docs include mapping + timeline
- [x] Tests updated

## Commits (squashed)
1) telemetry: rename cache metric instruments + normalize labels
2) telemetry: add legacy alias emission helper + config flag
3) docs: add cache metrics migration mapping + deprecation timeline
4) tests: update integration assertions for canonical names

Merged via squash.

Related:
- Linear: ENG-4821 (finalize metric definitions/tags)
- Downstream dashboards: observability-pack PR-612 (panels) will be updated to canonical names after this lands
